summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on install and import
details: The package is published under an internal-looking scope (`@ecg-internal/js-react-i18n`) at an implausibly high version (99.0.1) with a stub main that only exports a Proxy no-op, consistent with a dependency-confusion squat targeting an internal registry name. On `npm install`, the `postinstall` hook runs `node beacon.cjs`; the main entry `index.js` runs the same beacon at require/import time. The beacon POSTs a JSON payload containing the installer's hostname, install path (`__dirname`), current working directory, Node version, and package coordinate to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint `http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc` over plain HTTP. The destination is not publisher-associated, is reached via a bare IP with no TLS, and is not caller-configurable; the collected fields are installer-side host identifiers shipped without consent.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
